task: Zotero is installed and a pre-seeded library is available at /home/user/Zotero/zotero.sqlite. Open Zotero and wait for the library to load. Using the existing library contents, export the references contained in the collection 'Reinforcement Learning' to a BibTeX file. Save the result to: /home/user/Documents/rl_export.bib. The exported file must exist, contain exactly one BibTeX entry, and that entry's title must contain 'Survey of RL Methods'. Leave Zotero open after completing the task.
task_grounding: Zotero is installed and a pre-seeded library is at /home/user/Zotero/zotero.sqlite. Launch Zotero and wait for the library to load. In the left collections pane, click on the existing 'Reinforcement Learning' collection so its items appear in the middle pane. Select all items in that collection (Ctrl+A) and export them to BibTeX format: File > Export Library... (or right-click the collection and choose 'Export Collection...'), choose 'BibTeX' as the format, and save the output to exactly /home/user/Documents/rl_export.bib (you may need to type the full path). After export the file /home/user/Documents/rl_export.bib must exist and contain exactly 1 BibTeX entry whose title contains 'Survey of RL Methods'. Leave Zotero running.

verification.description: BibTeX file contains the survey paper title

cli_feasibility.translation: Python script using SQLite: 1) Find collection by name, 2) Query all items in collection via collectionItems table, 3) Format each item as BibTeX, 4) Write to output file
cli_feasibility.reason: Exporting a collection to BibTeX is straightforward. The script queries the collectionItems junction table to get all items in the collection, then formats their metadata as BibTeX. This is what Zotero's export feature does internally.
